judged.note: MUST paginate sync results is kept, joined with the never-unbounded prohibition.

moved.sentence: Never request or deliver unbounded result sets.

judged.note: "Never request or deliver unbounded result sets" is kept word for word under the MUST rule.

moved.sentence: Use the server-assigned sync version as the cursor — not an offset.

judged.note: The sync-version cursor, "not an offset", is kept and becomes MUST.

moved.sentence: MUST use incremental sync in production.

judged.note: MUST use incremental sync in production is kept, together with its two exceptions.

moved.sentence: Full sync (transfer everything every time) is only acceptable for initial bootstrap or recovery after database corruption.

judged.note: Full sync is "only acceptable" for the two cases (initial bootstrap, recovery after corruption), kept word for word in the MUST rule.

moved.sentence: If using timestamps, use Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC) rather than wall-clock time.

judged.note: The condition (if using timestamps) and HLC over wall-clock time are kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: MUST implement exponential backoff with jitter for failed sync attempts.

judged.note: MUST exponential backoff with jitter for failed sync attempts is kept, joined with the tight-loop prohibition.

moved.sentence: Never retry in a tight loop.

judged.note: "Never retry in a tight loop" is kept word for word under the MUST rule.

moved.sentence: After N consecutive failures, enter a circuit-breaker state: stop attempting sync and resume only after a cooldown period or explicit user action.

judged.note: N consecutive failures, the circuit-breaker state, stopping sync attempts and both resume conditions (cooldown or explicit user action) are kept, at SHOULD.
